findings: thread_select own same-current shortcut requires state exactly4, no local/default runnable count and unbound or matching processor; queued choice has no equivalent own state/active recheck.
raw thread_select decrements queue count before unlock, while C renders count decrement after unlock; original ordering preserved.

enqueue clamps local unsigned bucket index to31, does not clamp stored T58; writes T0/T4 tail links, hint/count and T8 runq before unlock; own body does not validate prior queue membership or active/state.
setrun first hands thread to idle processor pending slot/state3, otherwise default or master runq; nonzero T184 selects master rather than dereferencing binding as selected runq.
set_pri removes old runq before writing original priority T58; only removed threads are requeued, with third argument choosing old runq or setrun-like paths; invalid priority clamp is local.

choose_thread/choose_pset_thread scan descending hint, remove head and clear T8/count; positive count with no bucket panics, optional post-removal scan lacks own lower gate and relies on count/list invariants.

syntactic NULL branches in three dequeue blocks contradict immediately preceding unchanged register comparison; not genuine NULL result paths under those local conditions, unlike stack free-list count/head disagreement.
choose_pset_thread consumes caller-held runq lock, falls back to idle-list registration and processor idle-thread pointer; idle worker takes pending state3 slot and invokes or retries selection.
stack_attach sets T2c and TSS EBP/ESP=stack+ff4, EIP=186f74, EBX continuation; detach clears T2c; stack_free preserves stack matching reserve T30.
stack_alloc_try removes cached header+12 or uses T30 reserve, returns0 if neither, no own new allocation; cache count/head consistency and freeStack/allocStack backing remain open.
thread_swapin mask100 becomes200 and enqueues once under state premise, mask200 no-op; worker allocates stack before thread lock, clears300 and setrun only if old bit4.

stack_handoff transfers old T2c to new, publishes active_threads and updates CR3/LDT/TSS/CR0, without own active_stacks/stack_pointers literal writes; existing shared-stack global agreement is a premise.
switch_context publishes new active_threads/active_stacks/stack_pointers and uses new TSS CR3; C omits CR3 and CR0 writes, selectors raw memory WORD loads versus fixed C constants.
__switch_tss has third stack cookie input lost by C, optionally saves callee registers/EBP/return EIP and post-POP ESP, restores new registers/ESP and JMPs saved EIP with cookie in EAX.
first stack trampoline PUSHes EAX cookie then CALLs restored EBX continuation and HLT loops on return; thread_continue uses cookie for dispatch then calls active T34 continuation.
raw direct caller and specified global literal-write survey is bounded, no alias/indirect/out-of-function or native scheduler fairness/safety proof.
